correctness.rationale: Any independent set on two or more shores must lie in one aligned deleted triple; the one- and two-mark weighted counts follow by the same split. This gives the normalized covariance z²F/Z², and complementing both occupation indicators leaves the covariance unchanged. The n=3 polynomial has positive linear and quadratic coefficients and the higher coefficients are nonnegative. For n=4 the leading coefficients through the positive linear term have one variation; for n≥5 the upper bounds for a3 and a4 are strictly negative (their parenthetical polynomial factors have positive coefficients after writing n=5+m). The j=5 coefficient is negative by the same check, and both binomial ratios to C(2n−2,j) decrease or vanish as j increases. This gives exactly one variation for F/z, with the one possible sign of a2 immaterial. Near zero F>0, and the top coefficient −1 for n≥4 forces a positive root, which is simple by the multiplicity version of Descartes. At z=x/n the uniform Taylor expansion follows by expanding (1+x/n)^{cn+d} on compact x intervals. The leading profile f0 has derivative −2 at L=log 2. Bracketing by its opposite signs near L is uniform in k; the expansion then gives nz_{n,k}−L=O(n⁻¹) and substitution gives correction f1(L;k/n)/(2n) with f1(L;k/n)=4L+(1+3k/n)L². The covariance limit follows with Z→3e^x−2.
